subject: Post-call: geo controls, PII routing, and backup constraints
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sara Bailey <sara.bailey@asterhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Oct 2025 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: geo controls, PII routing, and backup constraints

Hi Sara — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the three follow-up items you asked us to clarify: 

1) PII handling: you mentioned that PHI/PII must never leave US jurisdictions for your regulated workflows. We can pin inference for those routes to US-only capacity. Need to confirm whether logs containing request metadata (IP, timestamps, request IDs) are considered PII for Aster — if so we will ensure log retention is disabled for those routes or routed to your KMS-bound customer project.

2) Cross-region failover: you want warm standby in EU/APAC but only for non-PII workloads. For PII routes we propose a cold-standby restore where a backup snapshot is kept encrypted in your preferred region and can be restored within the RTO window. We outlined two options on the call; please confirm the preferred RTO and whether automated failover is allowed for non-PII.

3) Backups and retention: question on retention windows — you indicated a 90-day working-set retention for transaction traces but a 7-year archival requirement for certain records. We can configure short-term token-level cache + long-term encrypted object archive. We will need the exact retention buckets and whether Redwood-hosted archives are acceptable or if Aster requires customer-managed archival (S3 with their account).

Attached is a short questionnaire and a diagram that maps the proposals we discussed. Could you fill the questionnaire (particularly Q2 on what Aster classifies as PII in this integration) and return it? Once we have that, Aditya and Monica will scope a formal security-runbook and cost delta for pinning + cold backup.

Next steps we propose:
- Sara: complete questionnaire and confirm RTO for PII workflows (by EOW if possible)
- Aditya: prepare cost/throughput delta for US-pin + cold-standby plan
- Monica: prepare SOC2 artifact list and recommended audit log redaction options

Thanks — I’ll stand by for the questionnaire.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood-geo-residency-questionnaire-v1.docx (docx, 42 KB); pinning-diagram.png (image, 120 KB))

From: Sara Bailey <sara.bailey@asterhealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: AsterHealth Security Team <security@asterhealth.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Oct 2025 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: geo controls, PII routing, and backup constraints

Vanessa — thanks for the summary and the questionnaire. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- PII definition: for this project Aster defines PII to include name, DOB, patient ID, and any direct identifiers. We also consider IP + session identifiers to be pseudonymous telemetry that must be treated with the same controls if they can be correlated back to a patient.

- Failover policy: automated failover is acceptable for non-PII only. For PII workflows we require human-approved failover (we have a runbook and ops on-call that will trigger). Our desired RTO for PII is 8 hours, RPO 24 hours.

- Backups: archival must be in encrypted storage under our AWS account for any data classified as regulated. Short-term caches (less than 30 days) can be Redwood-managed but must have logging disabled for PII routes.

I can fill the questionnaire but need two clarifications on Q4 and Q7 before I complete it (see inline in the doc). Can you have Aditya or Monica call out how logging redaction would work at ingestion?

Sara
Director, Integrations & Security
AsterHealth

On Wed, Oct 15, 2025 at 08:50 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for your time this morning — sending the questionnaire now.

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sara Bailey <sara.bailey@asterhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Oct 2025 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: geo controls, PII routing, and backup constraints

Sara — appreciate the quick clarifications, that RTO/RPO profile is helpful and matches our expectation for a cold-standby model. Quick answers to your two asks: 

- Logging redaction at ingestion: Redwood can perform field-level redaction on request bodies and metadata before writing to any indexed logs. For PII routes we propose a two-tier approach: 
  a) Ingestion-time redaction: key fields (name, DOB, patient_id) are removed/masked at the edge and replaced with non-reversible hashes; IPs can be removed entirely.
  b) Audit bundle: where required for investigations we can write encrypted audit bundles to an S3 bucket in your AWS account (customer-managed keys) that contain full request/response and context; access is gated via your IAM and a formal request flow.

- Attachment Q4/Q7: Monica has flagged recommendations on where to put redaction hooks in the pipeline and an example regex whitelist for allowed telemetry. 

We attached a redline-friendly questionnaire with notes in Q4/Q7 and a diagram showing the cold-standby snapshot cadence. Can you confirm whether we should mark the backup snapshot as "customer-owned encrypted archive" or "Redwood-hosted encrypted archive" for the 7-year items? If you choose customer-owned, we will include S3 config steps in the runbook.

Thanks — I’ll get Aditya to scope the cost implication and send a short breakdown by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Vanessa

(Attachment: redwood-geo-residency-questionnaire-v1.docx (docx, 43 KB) — with inline notes)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Oct 2025 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call: geo controls, PII routing, and backup constraints

Looping in my quick estimates here so we can get ahead of the ask to Sara. High-level notes: 

- US-pin for PII routes (dedicated reserved capacity): estimated premium ~+22% on token cost due to reserved US-only pool and smaller effective batching. Will provide a per-100k-token delta in the runbook.

- Cold-standby snapshots: weekly encrypted snapshots to a customer-owned S3 (if Aster chooses that option) meet the 24-hour RPO and 8-hour RTO if automation is limited to manual restore. The incremental storage cost is modest; restore labor is the main operational cost.

- Logging/redaction: implementing ingestion-time redaction adds ~0.5–1ms overhead per request in the pipeline; if Aster requires hashing + audit bundle creation to customer S3, add a small per-request egress and KMS cost.

I will prepare a short cost/ops table and a JSON config snippet that shows how to toggle pinning per-route and how to mark a route as "PII-protected" which enforces log redaction + customer-archive only. Sending draft by EOD.

Cheers,
Aditya
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
